question: Should OpenClaw adopt first-declared exact-path ownership, with only the documented tool-policy exceptions, as the supported V1 authority model for ordered configuration layers?
rationale: The proposal is technically coherent and demonstrated in a real lifecycle, but choosing layer authority and allowable monotonic changes defines a durable security and compatibility contract that automation cannot approve.

options.title: Approve the V1 authority model
options.body: Accept the generic startup-only model while requiring the implementation to preserve ordinary no-flag behavior and reject weakening conflicts.

options.title: Narrow the exception set
options.body: Retain ordered layers but revise or remove monotonic exceptions until each security-sensitive rule has explicit owner approval.

options.title: Defer managed layers
options.body: Leave composition in host integrations until OpenClaw adopts a broader configuration-control-plane direction.

recommendation.title: Approve the V1 authority model
recommendation.body: Accept the generic startup-only model while requiring the implementation to preserve ordinary no-flag behavior and reject weakening conflicts.

likelyOwner.reason: The explicit mention and subscription at the maintainer-review transition is the strongest available signal for ownership of the product-level core boundary decision.
